debate_title: AI governance frameworks for advanced AI systems

conflicts.point: Whether hardware-level telemetry and cryptographic modules can effectively decouple safety oversight from proprietary silicon manufacturing gatekeeping.

positions.stance: Hardware security modules integrated post-fabrication allow independent third parties to verify cluster throughput and training boundaries without routing inspections through proprietary foundry lines.

Post-fabrication hardware modules rely on proprietary microcode and cryptographic keys controlled exclusively by advanced semiconductor manufacturers, meaning hardware attestation replaces government gatekeeping with a corporate manufacturing monopoly.

conflicts.point: Whether the risks of unconstrained frontier AI model development outweigh the human costs and medical delays caused by pre-deployment regulatory friction.

positions.stance: Preventing irreversible, catastrophic public safety failures justifies mandatory pre-deployment checks and administrative delays regardless of market friction or near-term innovation slowdowns.

Pre-deployment regulatory delays create immediate, measurable human costs by slowing life-saving medical research and technological progress, which outweighs speculative or hypothetical catastrophic risks.

verdicts.conflict: Whether hardware-level telemetry and cryptographic modules can effectively decouple safety oversight from proprietary silicon manufacturing gatekeeping.
verdicts.rationale: Both positions rely on structural assertions about semiconductor supply chains without empirical deployment data from current frontier clusters. The safetyist position assumes technical auditability is neutral, while the skeptic assumes microcode control guarantees monopoly capture, leaving implementation feasibility unproven.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Independent security audits of deployed cryptographic attestation modules on commercial AI accelerators operating at scale.

verdicts.conflict: Whether the risks of unconstrained frontier AI model development outweigh the human costs and medical delays caused by pre-deployment regulatory friction.
verdicts.rationale: This disagreement weighs incommensurable values: the low-probability, high-consequence risk of systemic safety failures against the continuous, diffuse costs of administrative delay on downstream innovation. Neither camp provides an empirical conversion rate between compliance friction and delayed medical breakthroughs.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Empirical quantification of compliance delays in comparable dual-use technology sectors paired with calibrated risk assessments of frontier model misalignments.
